chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said: Ten people were sitting, and in the middle of them was a bag containing a thousand dirhams. So some of them asked others, 'Is this bag yours?' So all of them said, 'No.' And one of them said, 'It is for me.' So [I asked], 'For whom is it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'asws ) said: 'For the one who claimed it.'
ai.seo_question: How is ownership of found property determined in Shia jurisprudence according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a legal principle regarding found property, ruling that the claim of a single individual prevails over the silence of the group, thereby emphasizing the importance of active assertion of rights. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential approach to resolving ambiguity in ownership by prioritizing the explicit claimant, a concept relevant to both individual possession and communal economic interactions.
